extra.reason: Superseded by landed work: DICT/README.md documents the JSONL schema (required word/pos/gloss_en; optional gloss_fr/root/morphology/source) and DICT/entries.jsonl ships 2911 conforming entries (main 514ca3e, PR #5).
Superseded by landed work: GRAMMAR/grammar.md has the chapter structure (Fundamentoj, Morfologio, Sintakso, Fonologio/Ortografio, Pragmatiko) plus GRAMMAR/index.md (main 50b54a0, PR #3).
tools/normalize_corpus.py normalizes all 89 RAW/ sources into CORPUS/ with a per-source manifest.
43 sources added (30 Gutenberg, 13 Vikifontaro whole books); archive.org evaluated and rejected with the finding recorded.
Skipped per owner decision: quarantined in QUARANTINE/, excluded from the corpus, provenance and rationale recorded.
Pipeline built, run, and verified; 518 lemmas accepted with glosses and citations. Long tail and the lemma/inflection policy question tracked separately.
Guide rewritten with verified corpus citations; three substantive errors corrected and divergences documented.
Resolved: corpus now uses the union of the source-country (life+70, Wikidata-verified) and US (95-year) terms; 10 further books added.
Settled: productive derivations earn entries and are surfaced for review as their own lemmas; the underlying peel_affixes bug that caused most of the disagreement is fixed.
Round 2 done; dictionary at 5127 entries. Remaining tail tracked by the same re-runnable mechanism.
O'Connor parsed and merged: 5935 new entries, a 12497-headword English index, and 56 affix segmentation examples.
Triaged: 3 quarantined, 3 excluded from mining, the rest kept with the evidence recorded in RAW/QUALITY.tsv.

Replaced the diacritic-ratio proxy with a measured gate (conversion_is_sound): convert only if the substitution turns more distinct spellings into Esperanto words than it breaks. Fixes pg-24575 (now converted, 63.8%->70.0% recognisable), keeps the English/French Ekzercaro translations unconverted, and newly rejects pg-60429, whose 104 'digraphs' were all in the English licence.

Fixed in tools/normalize_corpus.py: repair_mojibake runs before slicing. 2504 diacritics recovered; pg-60429 now scores 97.7% recognisable and 18773 tokens of Goethe enter the corpus as Esperanto instead of replacement characters. Only one RAW source is affected; the detector is general and gated at 20 runs.

Implemented as mine_lemmas.line_is_foreign: a recognisability floor per line plus a curated list of foreign function words for lines too short to score. Unknown candidates per shard fell from 1633-2118 to 781-1271 while derived lemmas dropped 2%; the words that disappeared were the(693), of(337), that(90), be(82). Reviewers in the following round reported foreign leakage down to 7-41 of 320, nearly all single words quoted inside Esperanto sentences, which no per-line rule can catch.

Fixed and re-extracted. resolve_template no longer filters on the last-argument path, so {{SIC|c|C}}ezaro yields Cezaro; alignment keywords are dropped only when another argument survives; a lone argument is content; measurements never are. Also added the missing {{Lingvo}} alias (552 uses) and fixed the page-break hyphenation pair {{vdk}}/{{vdf}}, which had been returning only the second half of every split word. Standalone 'ezaro' is now 0 (was 113); 'la la' is 3 (was 105, against 7 in volume II); 'demandos' is whole again.

Root cause found and fixed upstream, not patched: the wikitext reads {{SIC|c|C}}ezaro 132 times — Wikisource editors marking that the book prints a lowercase initial — and our template resolver filtered both arguments away as alignment codes. Verified against the dump's own wikitext. After re-extraction standalone 'ezaro' is 0. The 'la la' sequences in the same file had a second cause, the unrecognised {{Lingvo|la|frigidarium}}, also fixed: 105 down to 3.

load_vocabulary now contributes the stem of every whole word longer than three characters, so an entry promoted from the corpus is recognised in all its inflections. roots grew from about 16k to 22759. laŭtlegis, englutinta and enpaki now analyse as known in every shard rather than in whichever one happened to meet the infinitive first.

PREFIX gained the 22 prepositional prefixes (al, antaŭ, apud, ĉe, ĉirkaŭ, de, en, inter, kontraŭ, krom, kun, per, post, preter, pri, pro, sen, sub, super, sur, tra, trans) and SUFFIX gained -il and -ing. alkudri, surkudrita, entenata, altirata, trapasante and englutinta all resolve now.

The compound test now runs on the stem as well as the whole token, allows the connecting vowel (vent-o-montrilo) and strips the second root's own ending. banlokoj, batalkampojn, sidloko, laborilo and ventomontrilo all resolve. Audited the result: of 7198 lemmas accepted only by this rule, a random sample is almost entirely genuine compounds, but the highest-frequency ones were proper names accepted as compounds (Vinicii as vin+icii, 910 occurrences), so the name rule now overrides the morphology when a lemma appears capitalised more than once and never in lower case.

Added esperanto.participle_infinitive, used by the miner rather than by citation_form. Only the adjectival and adverbial participles are reduced: reducing the nominal ones turned vizito into 'vizi', soldato into 'soldi' and komitato into 'komiti', and no vocabulary check catches that, because sold- is a root and Esperanto really would build 'soldi' from it. Verified on all 18 forms the reviewers cited and on 12 nouns that must be left alone.

mine_lemmas.normalise_token now resolves the three constructions separately: the elided article is dropped (l'homaro -> homaro), Zamenhof's morpheme-separated spelling is joined when the result is recognisable (inter'naci'e -> internacie, frat'in'o -> fratino), and eye-dialect elision is rejected outright (h'm, n'nio, 'strordinare). dank' al is kept as written, since the apostrophe there elides an ending in a fixed expression.

Fixed: the threshold moved from the map to the reduce, where the counts from all shards are summed. Also fixed the related keying defect that exposed it — shard records were keyed by the analysed root ('banlok'), which is not a word and not what any reviewer had seen, so improving the morphology moved the key and orphaned 917 approved lemmas. Records are now keyed by the word's own citation form. The lost verdicts were recovered by merging the committed ledger with the 211 raw reviewer batch files: 8091 verdicts, 5218 of them 'lemma'.

Already fixed by the vdk/vdf repair in round 4, and the diagnosis in this bead was wrong about the cause. The orphan halves were not text dropouts: eo.wikisource marks a word split across a page break with {{vdk|head|tail}} at the foot of one page and {{vdf|head|tail}} at the head of the next, and the resolver returned only the tail from both. All 12 forms the reviewer named are now 0 occurrences (tino, rimentado, gnaĵo, ciza, trante, kuteble; ĉeco and stre were grep artefacts matching inside feliĉeco and dekstre). What does remain is 165 page-gap splice points across the qualifying books, where the quality gate drops an unproofread page between two kept ones — Robinsono Kruso has 34, most books 1-3. Those lose whole sentences, not word halves, and each file's header records the count ('448 proofread pages of 458 scanned'), so the loss is visible rather than silent.

Added 'numeral' and 'nonce' to the closed verdict set in review_shard.py, with the reasoning documented in the docstring reviewers read first. Neither promotes, so they record a judgement without growing the dictionary. In use from round 5.

Fixed at the source rather than in citation_form: mine_lemmas.foreign_spans now skips a parenthesis of two to four tokens in which nothing is recognisable Esperanto, so the binomial never reaches citation_form to be mis-analysed. The parenthesis pattern alone cannot decide it — the same shape holds Esperanto stage directions, (Vilhelmo silentas), (Volas iri) — but recognisability inside the span can, and one recognisable word keeps the whole span. Measured over the mined corpus: 517 spans, 730 distinct tokens, comprising the Latin binomials (Abies pectinata, Ascaris lumbricoides, Buphagus africanus), translator credits (translated by Clarence Bicknell), currency notes and citation shorthand (ibid, pp, Oxon). Takes effect at the next re-mine.

Fixed by tools/repair_headwords.py: 1466 comma-joined headwords truncated at the comma with the original string kept in revo_raw, 13 with a bibliographic reference glued on dropped and listed, 205 duplicates that truncation exposed collapsed keeping the better-sourced entry, 5 glosses stripped of a leaked ReVo officialness marker. Every headword in entries.jsonl is now a single word: 0 with a comma, 0 with a space. The second variant is NOT reconstructed — see esp-1u4 for why and for what a re-merge needs to do.

Fixed in the same pass. The eight were case variants from two sources, not a judgement call: the Fundamento capitalises a proper noun and ReVo does not. Each pair is merged keeping the Fundamento spelling, and a sense the losing entry had is carried across rather than dropped — Dio is now 'God; god' and Pasko 'Easter; Passover'. Seven more pairs of the same shape turned up once truncation exposed them (Aprilo/aprilo,o and the other month names), so 15 in total. Duplicate headwords in entries.jsonl: 0.

All 45 cells present. tools/complete_correlatives.py generated the six missing ones from the grid — nenial, neniom, ties, ĉial, ĉies, ĉiom — tagged source: correlative-grid so the provenance stays honest about being generated rather than attested.

tools/link_grammar.py adds a 'grammar' field to the 181 entries a gloss cannot serve alone: 45 correlatives, 48 affixes and endings, 88 articles, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, particles and numerals. Mapping is by part of speech and by the correlative pattern, never by a hand-written word list, so it stays correct as the dictionary grows, and load_sections exits rather than writing if a heading it targets has moved.
